 Bay Area food banks ramp up operations ahead of holiday season 
 The California Department of Food and Agriculture reports that one in five Californians is struggling with food insecurity. 
 By Damian Trujillo • 
 Published 3 hours ago • 
 Updated 3 hours ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 The San Francisco-Marin Food Bank is ramping up its operations for the holiday season. Damian Trujillo reports. 
 Bay Area food banks are seeing an increased need as the holiday season approaches.
 At the San Francisco-Marin Food Bank, operations are kicking into overdrive.
 Watch NBC Bay Area News free wherever you are
   WATCH HERE 
 "During the holidays, we serve the same number of households that we do in the spring," said Katy Mann with the San Francisco-Marin Food Bank. "But during the holidays, we also ensure that we are sending a double protein, a double grain to make sure that our families have enough at their holiday table."
 For the Porciuncula family, the San Francisco-Marin Food Bank has been a lifesaver.
 "I work full-time, but we still don’t have enough money to pay for food that we need on a daily basis," Craig Porciuncula said.
 The family of five is having a hard time making it in the Bay Area. They get their weekly groceries at the food bank.
 "After payday within two to three days, we’re down to zero," Porciuncula said. "We're trying to make it through the week."
 The California Department of Food and Agriculture reports that one in five Californians is struggling with food insecurity. That’s roughly 8.8 million people in the state.
 At the San Francisco-Marin Food Bank, that need skyrocketed during the pandemic, and it hasn’t let up.
 "Living in San Francisco, the economic disparity is huge and so visible," Mann said. "It makes me really proud to do my job and to work here, to know that the work that I do every day, the work that our staff does, that our volunteers do, ensure that we're doing our best to help the one in five in our community who are at risk of hunger."
